title: Road Trip Diary, Day One
text:
Today we started our road trip to Aunt Bea's farm. Dad packed the car at six in the morning. He packed two suitcases, a cooler, and {number} {plural noun}, just in case.

Mom held the map on her lap. She said we had to turn left at the big {noun} and then drive {adverb} until we saw a sign for {place}. My little brother Theo asked if we were there yet about every two minutes.

For lunch we stopped at a picnic table by a lake. I ate a sandwich with {food} in the middle. Dad said it was the most {adjective} sandwich he had ever seen.

At night we stayed at a hotel with a pool shaped like a {noun}. Theo and I {past tense verb} in the water until our fingers got wrinkly. Tomorrow we drive the rest of the way, and Aunt Bea says the first thing we will do is {verb} with her goats.

title: Greetings from Echo Canyon
text:
Dear Grandpa, greetings from Echo Canyon! We drove here in Mom's blue car. It took {number} hours, and we only stopped once to look at a {adjective} cow.

The canyon is very deep and very orange. When you yell into it, it yells back. I yelled {silly word}, and the canyon yelled it back {adverb}. A park ranger named Mr. Hall told us the rocks are millions of years old and are mostly made of {plural noun}.

Today we went on a short hike on a flat, safe trail. Dad wore his big hat with a {noun} on top. We saw a lizard {verb ending in ing} on a warm rock, and Mom took a picture of it.

I bought you a present at the gift shop. It is a tiny {noun} in a glass jar, so please keep it somewhere {adjective}. Tomorrow we are going to {verb} at the visitor center, and I will tell you all about it. Love, June

title: Rules for the Back Seat Spotting Game
text:
This is the official spotting game for our family van. Everyone in the back seat can play. Grown-ups who are driving may not play, because they need to look at the road.

Here is how it works. When you see a red car, you say {exclamation} and get one point. When you see a truck carrying {plural noun}, you get five points. If you spot a cow wearing a {noun}, you win the whole game right away.

You are not allowed to {verb} while you are spotting. You must also keep your {body part} inside the car at all times. If you yell too {adverb}, you lose a point, and Mom will give you a {adjective} look.

The winner gets to pick the music for one hour. Last week my sister won, and she picked a song about {verb ending in ing} {plural noun}. We listened to it {number} times.

title: Snacks Packed for the Long Drive
text:
Mom made a snack list for our drive to the beach. She taped it to the cooler so nobody would forget anything.

The front pocket has apple slices, cheese sticks, and a bag of {adjective} {plural noun}. The cooler has water bottles, yogurt cups, and one big jar of {food} for Dad. Dad says he needs it to drive {adverb}.

The secret bag under my seat has crackers shaped like a {noun} and {number} {plural noun} that Grandma sent. Grandma says to only open the secret bag if somebody starts {verb ending in ing}.

The snack rules are on the back of the list. Please do not {verb} with your food. Crumbs must stay in the car, not in your {noun}. Whoever finishes first has to tell everyone a story about a {adjective} sandwich.

title: Things Dad Packed in the Trunk
text:
Before every trip, Dad makes a list of everything in the trunk. He says a good traveler is a {adjective} traveler. Here is his list for this year.

One tent, folded very flat. Two sleeping bags, rolled up tight. One spare tire and a box of {plural noun} for emergencies. A pillow for Mom, a blanket for me, and a tiny {noun} for my baby sister. Last of all, his lucky {noun}. Dad has brought it on every trip since he was {number} years old. He says it helps him {verb} when the road is bumpy.

At the very bottom of the trunk is a mystery box. Dad will not tell anyone what is inside. When I shook it, it went {sound} and something inside {past tense verb}. Mom just smiled {adverb}.

When we got to the campsite, Dad finally opened the mystery box. Inside was a big pile of {plural noun}. Dad said that is what every camper needs.

title: Welcome to the Sunny Hills Rest Stop
text:
Welcome to the Sunny Hills Rest Stop! We are happy you stopped to stretch your legs. Please read these signs before you explore.

Our picnic tables are painted green and are perfect for eating {plural noun}. The water fountain is next to the big {noun}. It works best if you ask it {adverb}.

Our dog area is behind the fence. Dogs may sniff, run, and {verb}, but they may not chase the {plural noun}. We also have a friendly {animal} named Biscuit who lives by the gate. Biscuit enjoys {verb ending in ing} and being told he is {adjective}.

The gift shop sells maps, hats, and a snow globe with a tiny {noun} inside. Our most popular item is a T-shirt that says "I Stopped at Sunny Hills and All I Got Was a {adjective} {noun}." Thank you for visiting. Please wave {adverb} as you drive away.

title: The Traffic Report on Radio Five
text:
Good morning, drivers! This is Penny Park with your traffic report from Radio Five. Traffic on Main Street is moving slowly this morning because a farmer is walking {number} {plural noun} across the road. Please wait {adverb} and wave hello to them.

On the highway, a truck carrying {food} is driving very carefully up the hill. The driver is waving at everyone. Over on Oak Bridge, there is a man {verb ending in ing} in a {adjective} costume. We do not know why, but he looks very happy.

The weather today is sunny with a small chance of {plural noun} in the afternoon. If you are driving to the lake, remember to bring a {noun} and your sunglasses.

That is all for now. Stay safe, buckle up, and remember to {verb} every time you see a yellow car. Back to you, Bob!

title: Dear Grandma, We Are Almost There
text:
Dear Grandma, we are on our way to your house! I am writing this letter in the back seat, so sorry if my letters are wiggly. We have been driving for {number} hours. So far I have counted seven horses, two windmills, and one very {adjective} {noun}.

Dad keeps singing the same song about {plural noun}. Mom says if he sings it one more time, she will {verb}. My cousin Sam fell asleep and is {verb ending in ing} with his mouth open. He is holding his favorite {noun} like a teddy bear.

We stopped for lunch at a diner. I ordered a grilled cheese, and it came with a side of {plural noun}. The waiter said it was the house special.

Please get your guest room ready. I am bringing my pillow, my toothbrush, and a {adjective} surprise. I think you will {verb} when you see it. Love, Maya

title: Mom's Directions to the Campground
text:
These are Mom's directions to Pine Tree Campground. Read them out loud to the driver one step at a time. First, drive down our street and turn right at the house with the {adjective} mailbox. Keep going until you see a gas station shaped like a {noun}. Wave at the man who sells {plural noun} on the corner. He always waves back.

Next, get on the long road and stay on it for {number} miles. You will pass a field full of {plural noun}. Do not stop to look at them, or we will be late for dinner.

When you see the sign with a picture of a {animal} wearing sunglasses, turn left. The road gets bumpy here, so drive {adverb}.

At the campground, look for the ranger named Lou. Tell him our family is here to {verb}. He will give us a map and a {adjective} welcome.

title: Rules for Riding in the Family Van
text:
Welcome to the Garcia family van. Before we leave the driveway, every passenger must read these rules.

Rule one: Everyone buckles up, even the {animal}. Rule two: Feet stay on the floor, not on your brother's {noun}. Rule three: The window may only be opened if you ask {adverb}.

Rule four: Nobody is allowed to {verb} until we get to the highway. Rule five: If you need a break, raise your hand and say the magic word, which is {silly word}. Rule six: Snacks must be shared. Last time, Abuela brought a whole bag of {plural noun} and gave the biggest one to the dog. Rule seven: Singing is allowed, but loud {verb ending in ing} is allowed only on Saturdays.

Rule eight: The driver is always in charge, and the driver today is Papa. He has driven this van for {number} years. Last summer he {past tense verb} the whole way to the lake. Please give him a {adjective} round of applause.
